metaDescription: Six divided plate picks in the mid budget, including a scoop-edge melamine plate and large 14 inch trays, compared on depth, heat limits and everyday use.
introParagraphs: A bit more budget opens up divided plates that do more than separate foods. In this range you can find a melamine scoop plate with non-slip pads, oversized trays with six or seven sections, and plate sets with lids that double as storage. The question to ask is no longer which plate is cheapest, but which feature you will use every day.

This guide covers six picks, starting with a scoop-edge plate with a tilt-inward rim and ending with a five piece set of 9 by 9 inch wheat straw plates. We evaluated each pick based on product specs and buyer feedback patterns, comparing size, depth, heat limits, what the maker says about the microwave and how much storage room each set needs. We left out serving trays meant for chips and dip because they are not dinner plates.

These are everyday home products, not medical devices. The scoop plate in the lineup has features that some people find easier for one-handed eating, but the maker's wording is about convenience and spill control. If you need clinical advice for eating or swallowing, speak with a professional, then use this guide to compare the plates themselves.

products.name: Ehucon Weighted Non-Slip Scoop Divided Plate
products.description:
The Ehucon plate is a melamine scoop plate with a two-section partition, a tilt-inward wide edge and non-slip pads under the base. The maker describes a glossy interior for easy cleaning and a matte exterior, with a heavy, solid weight that resists sliding when you push food with a spoon or fork. A concave edge and curved trailing edge guide food onto the utensil and gravy back into the plate.

This is the pick when sliding and spilling are the real problems, not food separation. The maker states it is not for microwave use, so reheating means using another dish. It is dishwasher safe and rated from minus 20 to 120 degrees Celsius without deformation. Only two sections are provided, so it is not a three-way portion plate like the PUPOPIK.

The listing mentions weighted utensils in the title, so check what is actually included in the set before you buy. Compared with the plastic 9 by 9 inch KANGYUN set, the Ehucon is heavier, steadier and designed for scooping, but it holds less variety and costs a plate at a time. Choose it for stability and a high-sided edge rather than for portion marking.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a heavy scoop plate with non-slip pads and a spill-guiding rim.

Tilt-inward edge helps guide food onto a spoon
Dishwasher safe with a -20 to 120 C range

products.name: DYB DONGYONGBAO 14 Inch 3 Piece Divided Plates
products.description:
DYB makes a very large plate, 14 by 10 inches, sold in a set of three in black, white and gray. Each plate has five deep compartments, and the maker says it is meant for a variety of foods and a balanced diet. The material is wheat straw with food-grade polypropylene, rated up to 248 degrees Fahrenheit, and the listing says microwave and dishwasher safe.

The footprint is the biggest in this guide, which suits people who like a full spread on one plate, such as a main, two sides, fruit and a roll. It also means the plate needs a large cabinet shelf and a large dishwasher rack, and it may not fit in a small microwave. The black, white and gray colors look closer to a cafeteria tray than a bright kids set.

Three plates are fewer than the five of the KANGYUN set, so this pick is more of a specialty plate than a household stock. Compared with the AIYoo 14 inch set, the DYB has five compartments instead of six, and the DYB listing does not include a utensil slot. Pick it for meal variety and a muted look.
products.bestFor: Big appetites that want five sections on one very large plate.
pros: 14 by 10 inch size is the largest here
Muted black, white and gray palette
cons: Only three plates in the set

products.name: AIYoo 14 Inch 4 Pack Six Compartment Plates
products.description:
AIYoo sells four 14 inch plastic trays in assorted colors, each with six compartments and a seventh space for utensils. The maker says the compartments are deep enough to keep food from spilling, and the trays are light, smooth, unbreakable and stackable. They can hold hot or cold food and are listed as microwave and dishwasher safe.

The heat statement is specific: a maximum of 248 degrees Fahrenheit for 5 minutes. That is a tighter instruction than most plates, so short reheating is fine but long cooking is not. Six compartments plus a utensil slot makes the tray work more like a buffet or lunch tray than a dinner plate, which is good for parties and snacks but crowded for a single large main.

Against the DYB 14 inch set, you get four trays instead of three and an extra section. The material is plain plastic rather than a wheat straw blend, so it feels more like a school tray. Choose this one for entertaining or for a household that wants tidy small portions of many foods.
products.bestFor: Parties, snack spreads and lunches with many small items.
pros: Six sections plus a utensil slot
Microwave and dishwasher safe use is listed
cons: Five minute heat limit is tight
Crowded for a single large main

products.name: PUPOPIK 10.5 Inch Wheat Straw Divided Plates
products.description:
PUPOPIK offers four 10.5 inch round plates with three compartments, made of wheat straw according to the listing. The maker calls them thick but light to hold, unbreakable and easy to clean with a smooth surface, and says they are stackable for picnics and travel. Microwave and dishwasher use are both stated.

The 10.5 inch round shape is the roomiest round plate in this lineup, and it fits a standard cabinet shelf better than the large DYB trays. The three compartments suit the classic main, starch and vegetable split, and the listing mentions portion control for adults. The material wording in the listing mixes wheat straw and melamine, so confirm the material before heating.

Compared with the 9 by 9 inch KANGYUN plates, the PUPOPIK gives more room per plate but fewer plates, four versus five. It is the practical pick if you want a plate that looks and stacks like a normal dinner plate. Expect a light plastic feel, easy handling and the usual top-rack dishwasher habit.
products.bestFor: Everyday dinners on a round plate that stacks like normal dishes.
pros: 10.5 inch round diameter has generous room
Stacks like a normal dinner plate
cons: Only four plates in the set

products.name: greenandlife 9 Inch Divided Plates with Lids 4 Pack
products.description:
The greenandlife set has four 9 inch plates with hard plastic lids so each plate becomes a storage container. The maker says the plates are deeper than earlier versions and made from wheat straw and food-grade polypropylene, with three compartments for portion control. The temperature rating goes up to 248 degrees Fahrenheit.

The lids are the value here. You can plate dinner, snap on the lid and refrigerate the whole plate, which reduces dirty containers and food waste. The listing says microwave, dishwasher and freezer safe, so a frozen plated meal can go straight into the microwave once the lid is vented or removed. Check the lid rating on the product page.

It is smaller than the PUPOPIK at 10.5 inches, and has fewer sections than the DYB trays, but it is the only pick with lids. The lids add steps to washing and take more storage room than bare plates. Choose it if you cook ahead or often have leftovers.
products.bestFor: People who plate leftovers and want one container that also serves dinner.
pros: Microwave, dishwasher and freezer use listed
cons: Lids add washing and storage bulk
9 inch size is smaller than the PUPOPIK

products.name: K Y KANGYUN 5 Piece 9 Inch Divided Plates
products.description:
KANGYUN sells five plates measuring 9 by 9 inches in pink, beige, green, gray and blue. They are made from wheat straw fiber, starch and food-grade polypropylene, with three compartments marked for 50 percent vegetables, 25 percent protein and 25 percent carbs. The listing mentions smooth round edges and says they are microwave and dishwasher safe up to 120 degrees Celsius.

The five piece set gives the most plates of any round option in this guide, which suits a couple who run the dishwasher every few days. The marked sections give a clear portion guide for people who want one. The 9 inch size is on the small side for a full dinner, so it works better for lighter meals.

Against the PUPOPIK at 10.5 inches, the KANGYUN is smaller but gives an extra plate and tighter color variety. Compared with the greenandlife lid set, it has no lids and no stated freezer rating, but the heat limit is clearly stated. It is a straightforward pick for everyday dishes without extras.
products.bestFor: Couples who want five plain divided plates with marked portions.
cons: 9 inch size is small for big dinners

buyingCriteria.explanation: Most divided plates are light and slide when you push food against them. The Ehucon scoop plate is the only pick here with non-slip pads and a heavy solid body, while the PUPOPIK and KANGYUN are light plastic. A non-slip mat under a light plate is a low-cost fix. If sliding is your main problem, choose the Ehucon.

Two sections, as on the Ehucon, suit a main with one side, three suit a classic meal, and five or six suit variety. The DYB has five and the AIYoo has six plus a utensil slot. More sections mean smaller sections, which can be too small for a large main. Choose the number that matches your normal plate.

The DYB 14 by 10 inch plate and the AIYoo 14 inch tray are large, while the KANGYUN is 9 by 9 inches. Large plates give room for a full spread but need wide shelves and rack space. A standard 10.5 inch round like the PUPOPIK fits normal storage. Measure your microwave before buying a 14 inch plate.

Makers differ: the AIYoo states 248 F for 5 minutes, the greenandlife and DYB state 248 F, the KANGYUN states 120 C, and the Ehucon is not for microwave use at all. Match the plate to how you reheat. Long reheating on a plate with a five minute limit risks warping. For daily microwave use, the greenandlife and DYB sets give the widest stated margin at 248 F.

A lid turns a plate into a container, which helps if you cook ahead. The greenandlife lid set is the one pick here with included lids and a listed freezer rating. Lids add an item to wash and store. Skip them if you do not save leftovers.

Wheat straw and PP plates like the PUPOPIK, DYB and KANGYUN are light and easy to stack, but can stain. Melamine like the Ehucon is heavier, glossy inside and easy to wipe. Both families go in the dishwasher, with plastic best on the top rack. Choose by weight preference and reheating needs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and grip
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at weight, pads and edge design based on product specs. The Ehucon leads with non-slip pads, a heavy body and a tilt-inward edge. Lightweight plastic plates scored lower for sliding.

howWeEvaluated.title: Sections and separation
howWeEvaluated.description: Section count and depth were compared across the lineup. The AIYoo leads with six plus a utensil slot, the DYB has five, and the PUPOPIK, greenandlife and KANGYUN have three. The Ehucon has two.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and storage
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared plate footprints with typical dinner portions and cabinet room. The DYB at 14 by 10 inches is the largest, and the KANGYUN at 9 by 9 inches is the smallest. Oversized plates lost points for storage.

howWeEvaluated.title: Heat and cleaning claims
howWeEvaluated.description: We read stated limits for microwave, dishwasher and freezer. The greenandlife and DYB state 248 F, the AIYoo gives a five minute cap, and the Ehucon is not for microwave use. Unclear claims were marked down.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pack value
howWeEvaluated.description: Pieces per set were compared with the plate's role. KANGYUN offers five plates, AIYoo and greenandlife and PUPOPIK four, DYB three and Ehucon one. A set scores best when the count matches the household.

faq.q: Which of these plates is best if food slides around?
faq.a: The Ehucon has non-slip pads, a heavy melamine body and a tilt-inward edge that guides food toward a spoon. The other picks are lighter plastic. A non-slip mat under any plate adds some grip.

faq.q: Can the Ehucon go in the microwave?
faq.a: No, the maker states it is not for microwave use. It is dishwasher safe and rated from minus 20 to 120 degrees Celsius. Reheat food in another dish and move it to the plate.

faq.q: How long can I microwave the AIYoo trays?
faq.a: The listing gives a maximum of 248 F for 5 minutes. That means short reheating is fine, but long cooking is not. Use a different dish for longer heating.

faq.q: Are large 14 inch plates practical at home?
faq.a: They suit people who like a full spread, but they need wide cabinet shelves, dishwasher racks and a big microwave. Measure your microwave turntable first. For normal storage, the 10.5 inch PUPOPIK is easier.

faq.q: Are the lids on the greenandlife set microwave safe?
faq.a: The maker lists the plates as microwave, dishwasher and freezer safe, but the lids are separate parts. Read the product page before heating with a lid on and vent it if you do. When unsure, remove the lid.

faq.q: Do portion marks on a plate actually help?
faq.a: A marked plate like the KANGYUN, with sections for 50 percent vegetables, 25 percent protein and 25 percent carbs, gives a visual guide at a glance. It does not change what you eat, and the sections are guidelines. Use it as a reminder, not a rule.

faq.q: Is a two section plate better than three?
faq.a: Two sections, as on the Ehucon, suit a main with a side and leave more room per section. Three sections suit a classic meal with a starch and a vegetable. Choose by how many items you plate.
